Technical summary / requirements (as captured in notes):
- Indexing scale: ~15M dense vectors today; expected growth to 45M in 12 months. Frequent re-indexing: weekly full rebuilds, hourly deltas for active repos. Must support streaming/upsert and efficient shard rebalancing.
- Query pattern: code search + semantic QA. Typical QPS in production target = 120 QPS, peak bursts to 800 QPS for nightly CI indexing triggers.
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 150ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 500ms for single-stage retrieval+rerank (for 10-100 candidate sets).
- Cost sensitivity: target cost/query $0.003 - $0.01 including embedding lookup + rerank. High sensitivity to GPU time for cross-encoder reranker.
- Model profile: prefer open LLMs (gpt-like alternatives) with 16-70B quantized variants. Proposal: sparse retrieval + bi-encoder at 384-1024 dim, then cross-encoder (small-medium) for top-50 rerank. Looking for Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/kv-cache quantization tradeoffs.
- Security/compliance: Must support SSO/SAML with Okta, SCIM provisioning, enterprise audit logs shipped to Splunk, KMS integration for key control, per-tenant data residency (EU/US).

POC observations / engineering notes:
- Reranker: current cross-encoder on Dedicated pool produced best accuracy but cost blowout; estimated $0.06/query at current scale for cross-encoder on CPU fallback. Need vector-first rerank + distilled cross-encoder for cost.
- Indexing: full rebuild time ~10 hours on their current infra; delta upserts are efficient but introduce hotspotting on a handful of shards. Suggested mitigations: workload-aware sharding, background compaction, and prioritized rebalancing.
- Caching: prefix + KV caching reduced token generation cost by ~18% in test flows. Redwood Optimize recommended adaptive batching windows during nightly runs to amortize kernel startup.
- Fallbacks: want automatic fallback to a cheaper model family under saturation (dedicated -> hosted small quantized variant). Discussed routing policy and data isolation needs.
